defaults.aboutTitle: Controversy is a discipline, not a season.
defaults.about:
Axiom is a tax controversy practice. We represent individuals and closely held businesses in IRS and state examinations, Independent Office of Appeals, and collection due process.

The first sitting is a reading of the notice — statute, year, and what they actually asked. We do not guess. We build the file the examiner will have to respect.
defaults.missionStatement: The notice is not the conclusion. It is the start of a record.

faqs.question: Should I call the number on the letter?
faqs.answer: Not before we read it. Deadlines matter. Improvised phone calls rarely help.

faqs.question: Do you handle state exams?
faqs.answer: Yes. We coordinate federal and state so one file does not create the other.

faqs.question: Will you speak for me?
faqs.answer: Yes. Form 2848 is the first filing. You are copied. You are not left in the room alone.

faqs.question: How are you paid?
faqs.answer: A written engagement after the notice review. We do not quote until we know the year and the issue.

defaults.blogSectionSubtitle: Exams, statutes, and what a notice actually means

newsPosts.title: Notice intake within 48 hours
newsPosts.excerpt: Send the PDF. We return a statute map and a next step.
newsPosts.body: Do not call the number on the letter first. Send the notice. We will tell you the deadline and whether a power of attorney should go out the same day.
newsPosts.author: Intake

blogPosts.title: What a CP2000 is — and is not
blogPosts.excerpt: A matching notice is not an assessment. Treat it like one and you invent the tax.
blogPosts.body: A CP2000 proposes a change based on third-party reports. It is not a bill until you let it become one. The reply is a record, not a phone script.
blogPosts.author: Axiom

blogPosts.title: Do not sign the first extension
blogPosts.excerpt: Time is the only leverage most taxpayers have. Spend it on purpose.
blogPosts.body: An extension can be useful. It can also be a gift to a thin exam. We decide after we know what they still need.
blogPosts.author: Axiom
